quality.scope: Local HTTP fixture/native Worker/app/WebGL/export. No independent real-SDK framebuffer readback.

limits: Cross-page coverage is point pages: 88000 points span two65535-capacity pages, lines and rectangle triangles each remain in one page.
Quality still uses identity transport and a local renderer; real-SDK framebuffer, alarm LOD and half-batch cancellation are not newly covered.

metricDefinitions.p95Method: Nearest rank within each run over consecutive ACK postMessage times, then median across runs within same group

limitations: Synthetic business records on one host; sdk=true means a real Baidu basemap, not real device observations. No location search requests were made.
Native Edge was headless. requestAnimationFrame callback cadence is not physical displayed FPS; no frame-presentation or independent GPU-completion timer is used.

First draw is first nonempty business GL draw submission. dataDone is Worker completion arrival after final ACK; lifecycle total adds the app completion wait. Neither is physical display presentation.
ACK interval P95 uses consecutive main-thread ACK post timestamps, excludes start-to-first ACK, and applies nearest rank ceil(0.95*n)-1. Group values are medians of per-run P95, not a pooled P95.
Bulk workload updates 2048 feature IDs, including point/line/rectangle IDs. It is not 2048 point-only devices; the existing API assigns the same xy to all currently bound vertices of each ID.

Two small calls and six bulk calls are accumulated separately per run. CPU measures update API execution; commit wall includes CPU plus awaitCommit scheduling and upload submission, not GPU completion. Rounded zero does not mean free work.

cpuGeometryBytes and gpuOwnedBufferBytes are renderer-owned allocations, not total process RAM/VRAM. Live-bounds typed arrays are extra and listed separately; strings, ID maps, Worker copies and SDK allocations are outside these counters.

Local performance alternates identity/gzip/identity with three different seeds. Do not pool its three rounds as one repeated distribution. SDK fast and paced each use identity and three paired seeds; only same-scope same-repeat comparisons are paired.

SDK runs use ordinary product start/resetView, without the formal loading benchmark camera-settle gate. SDK camera reset scheduling and basemap work are part of the observed chain; this is not a strictly frozen-camera causal benchmark.

Whole-model CPU hashes match between variants for every paired material. Independent full-RGBA quality checks use the local renderer and same shader with spatial selection disabled for the oracle, not independent SDK pixel proof.
No universal winner or statistical significance is claimed. Cold first current runs are retained, including 121ms and 103ms Long Tasks in SDK fast/paced.
Default adaptive LOD is disabled for equal-quality comparisons. Production runtime/default policy is unchanged; hybrid and bounds combinations are test instrumentation.
Known real-SDK forced WebGL context-loss whole-page reload remains unresolved. Export network-ambiguity retry and half-batch cancellation are outside this new quality matrix.

recommendations.reason: Best supported low-overhead general default: fast SDK throughput candidates do not also improve paced or local cases.

recommendations.scope: real SDK fast identity, million synthetic records
recommendations.choice: hybrid candidate when early response matters; large candidate when completion dominates
recommendations.reason: Hybrid reduces paired total by 17.51%..26.93% while starting earlier than fixed8192. Fixed8192 has the lowest total median here; its first submission is later.
Total is supply-limited and candidates are slightly slower; hybrid increases ACK interval P95 from about34.1ms to129.1ms, fixed8192 also delays first submission.
Extra1,373,208 typed-array bytes at million records and higher bulk-update CPU; no repeatable extra win over hybrid attributable to bounds in this workload.
